The Moroccan Royal Cabinet announced on Wednesday that King Mohammed has allocated 4 billion dirhams (€366 million) from the Hassan II Fund for Economic and Social Development to launch a national defence industry roadmap with 2035 as its target year. The plan's three stated goals are to create roughly 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, meet 40% of the Royal Armed Forces' and security services' equipment needs through domestic production by 2035, and generate more than 65% of defence-industry revenues from exports. Implementation is structured around a new strategic agency to carry out national defence industry policy and support investors, an industrial holding company to organize the production ecosystem and mobilize public and private capital, and two new defence-manufacturing zones in Ben Guerir and Benslimane—added to existing zones in Nouaceur and Sidi Yahya. The strategy draws on Morocco's automotive, aviation, and electronics expertise across priority areas including drones and autonomous systems, land and naval systems, defence electronics, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and dual-use technologies.

The roadmap is supported by international partnerships: Tata Advanced Systems (India) is cooperating to manufacture WhAP 8×8 armoured vehicles in Berrechid with a goal of increasing locally produced components; domestic firm MMI manufactures military turrets and remotely controlled weapon systems as an initial production base; and the Emirati group EDGE signed two agreements at the October Marrakech Air Show—one memorandum exploring local manufacturing of small arms and aircraft engines, and another covering supply of Desert Sting 16 and Thunder P-31 guided munitions to the Royal Moroccan Air Force. The king also directed establishment of a specialised academy for advanced training in partnership with industrial companies, plus a talent-channeling programme adapting vocational training to engineering, electronics, and digital needs.

As context, Stockholm International Peace Research Institute data place Morocco among Africa's leading importers of major weapon systems. No limitations or caveats were stated beyond these figures.
items.title: Morocco allocates €366 million toward a national defence-industry roadmap targeting 2035

items.summary: In Buea, capital of Cameroon's Southwest region, children displaced by the country's ongoing armed Anglophone conflict are resuming schooling but increasingly taking on market work to help their families survive. The crisis began in 2016 when teachers and lawyers protested over perceived marginalization of English-language education and common-law systems favoring French; this escalated into armed conflict between government forces and separatist groups seeking independence for the two English-speaking regions, commonly referred to as Ambazonia. UNHCR estimates that between 2.1 and 2.2 million people have been displaced due to the violence. At Buea's OIC Market, children from displaced families sell bleach, puff-puff, plantains, ginger, garlic, and oranges, particularly on weekends and before school. Fourteen-year-old Joy travels from Mutengene to Buea on weekends to sell sachets of bleach that her mother buys in bulk and repackages; she sells each for CFA 100 (about USD 0.17) with daily sales reaching CFA 10,000–15,000 (about USD 16.81–25.21). Fourteen-year-old Sidoine lost four years of schooling after her family fled Ekona when their house was burned; a well-wisher helped enroll her in Buea, though the family cannot permanently return to its farm. Younger children also contribute: twelve-year-old Michelle sells plantains while waiting for his mother from church, and Susan Achuagoh gives small quantities of oranges to sell while she stays at her stall after more than three years of interrupted schooling for her five children. Godiva Ndang epse Limene, Education and Partnerships Officer at Street Child UK-Cameroon, notes that prolonged exposure to armed violence may cause anxiety, difficulty concentrating, and social withdrawal, and warns that work consuming time needed for learning can affect cognitive, emotional, social, and physical development; she stresses that helping in a family business is not automatically child labor, with the distinction depending on age, activity nature and duration, risks involved, and whether it interferes with education, health, rest, or development. Education data cited by UNICEF from Regional Delegations of Basic Education figures dated September 2026 show that 223,749 children were completely out of school in the Northwest and Southwest regions, while 2,463 schools were non-operational—of which 2,005 were in the Northwest and 458 in the Southwest. Local partners including TeenAlive, FIED, SHUMAS, and AMEF support close to 100 Mobile Neighborhood Learning Corners and Satellite Learning Corners established in accessible locations such as village chiefs' homes, churches, schools, and community verandas; other interventions include school enrollment help, uniforms, learning materials, Teaching at the Right Level tutoring, Street Child's girls' resilience program with vocational training and mental health assistance, and FIFA Foundation-supported Play for Peace. Despite interruptions and added responsibilities, interviewed children retain ambitions—Eliot (14) wants to be an engineer, Sidoine hopes to study law though she worries about lost years, and Vickians (12), who sells miondo on weekends after fleeing Lebialem, studies computer science and aims to become a computer engineer. Southwest Governor Bernard Okalia Bilai stated at the start of the 2026–2027 academic year that authorities want children across the region equal access to education despite differences in school attendance between urban and rural communities.
items.title: Displaced Cameroon Children in Buea Balance Schooling with Market Work After a Decade of Anglophone Conflict

items.summary: Despite raising the most cash ever from an initial public offering and pricing above its target range, Anthropic PBC's stock plateaued after launching and fell about $6 by Friday's close, failing to lift sentiment in an AI trade that continued selling off. The Nasdaq 100 Index dropped 10% for the week—its worst performance since March 2020—as chipmakers led declines amid a looming Federal Reserve interest-rate hike and broader skepticism over whether technology is adapting to AI risks. Anthropic's underwhelming debut reinforced doubts about meeting lofty near-term expectations, according to Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors. Structural concerns compound the weakness: Democratic midterm gains raise fears that data center construction will slow as many candidates ran on blocking it, while higher rates increase capital costs for developers relying on credit markets—factors Malcolm Polley of Stratos Investment Management says constrain how AI-driven assets can be valued. Nvidia's turmoil added to investor unease after it ousted CEO Jensen Huang on Nov. 12 over an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China; despite strong earnings and a $150 billion buyback authorization, shares plunged 23% in the week (worst since 2008) and fell 48% from their Oct. 6 all-time high. Competitor Advanced Micro Devices also tumbled about 20% after short-seller questions raised concerns over its China business amid potential export restrictions. The selloff reflects skepticism toward hundreds of billions in computing-power spending that had driven the Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index to more than double in the first half of the year before losing 41% in the second half as cyclical fears resurfaced. Strategists remain divided: Brian Smedley of Cynosure Strategies expects the oversold market to stabilize and AI demand to stay strong, while Mark Luschini of Janney Montgomery Scott cautions that investors still lack clarity on what could catalyze gains and warns the selloff could deepen before stabilizing.
items.title: Wall Street Searches for a Catalyst After Anthropic IPO Fails to Rescue AI Trade

items.summary: Anthropic's stock fell about 9% from its Thursday debut close to $88.87, leaving a fully diluted valuation of roughly $1.6 trillion and a market capitalization of around $1.2 trillion based on shares outstanding. The decline raised questions about whether the company can sustain a valuation near 40 times sales over the past 12 months, which analysts say assumes years of rapid growth. Kaush Amin, head of private market investing at US Bank Asset Management, advised patience and evaluating Anthropic as it reports public results. Near-term volatility may persist as initial enthusiasm fades; options trading due to begin next week could add pressure, though London-based Intropic estimates index-tracking funds could buy up to 30% of shares by year-end, potentially supporting the stock later in the year.
items.title: Anthropic's Post-IPO Decline Signals Cooling for the AI Trade

items.summary: NASA announced that its Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day—about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers)—from Earth at 2:16 a.m. PST on Nov. 18, roughly 49 years after the probe launched Sept. 5, 1977. At this range, radio signals travel at light speed and take about 24 hours to reach the spacecraft and another 24 hours to return; NASA confirmed the milestone using a carrier signal rather than science data, which had not been received since Nov. 14 because of an ongoing technical issue that engineers are still analyzing. The mission is managed by JPL for Caltech, with Voyager 1 having become humanity's first spacecraft to cross into interstellar space in Dec. 2012 and its twin Voyager 2 following in 2018; both probes continue measuring the Sun's magnetic field while conserving power from their aging radioisotope thermal generators, which lose about 4 watts per year as plutonium depletes. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman commented on X that reaching one light-day is incredible and noted the spacecraft was built with 1970s technology; NASA officials Joe Westlake, Dave Gallagher, Linda Spilker, Suzanne Dodd, and Caltech president Ray Jayawardhana also weighed in on the mission's scientific contributions and engineering challenges. The article contains no stated forecast or explicit limitation beyond noting that science data transmission remains unresolved.
items.title: NASA's Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day from Earth After Nearly 49 Years of Travel

items.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanking him for his appeal urging citizens to avoid unnecessary gold purchases, stating the advice helped protect jewellers, traders, and investors from losses after a decline in gold prices. In a letter dated Sunday titled 'Your foresight saved lakhs of jewellers and investors from falling into debt,' CTI said the appeal had drawn criticism when first made but ultimately aided traders. According to the trade body, gold was priced at Rs 1.90 crore per kilogram when Modi issued his advice; it has since fallen to Rs 1.25 crore per kilogram, a decline of Rs 65 lakh per kilogram. CTI stated that had traders bought inventory at the earlier price, they would have incurred losses worth crores today, as jewellery traders typically maintain several months' stock and are exposed to significant downside risk. The organisation also noted that small online and offline gold dealers and stock market investors were similarly protected, with messages pouring into its groups thanking Modi for his advice. CTI added the price fall offered relief during a wedding season it said was witnessing 52 lakh weddings. The letter was signed by CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal and other office-bearers.
items.title: CTI Credits Modi's Gold Purchase Appeal for Averting Trader Losses

items.summary: Rising domestic airfares in India are preventing working migrants from traveling home for major life events during festival and wedding seasons. The increases stem largely from airlines citing higher fuel costs linked to the Iran war, making short-notice trips unaffordable—especially since trains are unavailable on demand. Clinical psychology student Aditi abandoned plans to fly from Delhi to Kolkata for 'bhai phota' after a Rs 23,000 round-trip fare; media professional Ananya Nair will watch her best friend's Dec 6 Kerala wedding online rather than pay an upward of Rs 30,000 round trip (cheapest direct morning flight from Delhi to Kochi at Rs 17,000 one-way); and first-time aunt Kavya missed her niece's July naming ceremony after a cheapest one-way fare of Rs 11,800. Salon professional Riya Sharma said the Jabalpur round trip exceeded 50% of her monthly income (cheapest flight at Rs 8,000 via Hyderabad), and Vasant could not attend his uncle's death in Bhubaneswar because fares approached Rs 27,000 for a round trip. A Times of India check on Nov 21 found one-way Delhi fares near Rs 20,000 at Christmas (Dec 25) and New Year's Day (Jan 1), with the highest prices in the Delhi-Bengaluru, Delhi-Kolkata, and Delhi-Ahmedabad sectors. Reduced seat availability—partly due to Air India cutting services on several routes—further pushed fares up; a Bengaluru-to-Patna one-way reportedly cost Rs 25,000 during Chhath Puja, prompting some travelers to use tempos with trains fully booked. The Supreme Court declined an urgent Nov 2 plea for a fare cap, noting petitioner claims of surges as high as 700% on some routes; Justice Vikram Nath dismissed the argument that air travel is essential by telling counsel 'Don't travel by air.' Findings are based on individual accounts and limited TOI fare checks rather than comprehensive data.
items.title: Sky-high Indian airfares force migrant families to miss weddings, births, and funerals

items.summary:
According to an interview with PTI published on November 22, 2026, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Ltd (MLMML) is considering a public listing in approximately 18 months. The company's Chairman Rajesh Jejurikar stated that the timeline remains broad and unconfirmed because MLMML has not finalized a listing date; he emphasized that management wished to avoid distraction from the IPO process. As of the interview, MLMML held an estimated valuation of around $1 billion with two investors on board and a third expected soon. Jejurikar noted that proceeds would be used partly for value unlocking but primarily to fund growth in new segments and products as well as capacity expansion, while Mahindra intends to retain its stake rather than significantly reduce it.

On product strategy, MLMML is targeting electric three- and four-wheelers across both passenger and cargo categories. Jejurikar clarified that the company would maintain its focus on last-mile urban transportation instead of intercity mobility, though he declined to specify particular products. Regarding demand trends, he observed that passenger electric three-wheelers had driven growth so far while cargo vehicles were expected to gain momentum.

For overseas expansion, MLMML is exploring Southeast Asia, Africa, and possibly Western markets, with Earthshot Prize recognition anticipated to facilitate global partnerships; however, Jejurikar cautioned that international entry would require time for assessing product suitability, business potential, EV penetration levels, and the development of distribution, spare-parts, and service ecosystems. He added that although the company received enquiries following the award, it had not yet conducted detailed work on its global strategy.

The text also notes a distinction between two awards: MLMML will use one million pounds from the Earthshot Prize to support women aspiring to become drivers rather than for business expansion. On pricing and incentives, Jejurikar explained that FAME and PM E-DRIVE subsidies were no longer available for this category, leaving only the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme; he attributed future pricing headroom to material cost optimization from higher volumes combined with customers recognizing EV economic benefits.

The report is grounded entirely in statements made by Jejurikar during the interview. Because these are reported claims rather than independently verified data, figures such as the $1 billion valuation and investor count should be treated as assertions attributed to their source.
items.title: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Chairman Signals IPO Within 18 Months Amid Product and Overseas Expansion Plans

items.summary: According to a Registrar of Companies filing published on November 22, 2026, Reliance Brands Ltd (RBL), a subsidiary of Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd that operates global fashion and lifestyle brands in India through partnerships, brand ownership, and retail operations, reported revenue from operations rising 3.77% to ₹3,390.89 crore for FY26, compared with ₹3,267.66 crore in FY25. The company narrowed its loss to approximately ₹137 crore (reported as ₹137.04 crore and ₹137.13 crore across the filing), down from a profit of ₹237.12 crore recorded in FY25, with last year's prior-year comparison figure cited at ₹233.79 crore loss. The company manages a portfolio spanning luxury, bridge-to-luxury, premium, and high-street fashion, plus F&B, eyewear, home & lifestyle, and toys, serving an estimated 12–15 million affluent Indian consumers. As of March 31, 2026, RBL operated 1,085 Points of Sale across India through proprietary concepts such as The Whitecrow, The Books & Café, and Tank, alongside over 90 partner brands. During FY26 the company added three global master franchise partnerships—Stella McCartney, MAX&Co, and Kurt Geiger—and entered athleisure with Fabletics; it also holds six subsidiaries, 11 joint ventures, four associate companies, and owns Hamleys, a toy retailer operating in 13 countries. The figures are drawn from the company's RoC filing and financial data accessed via Tofler, though some values differ slightly between sources within the report.
items.title: Reliance Brands Reports FY26 Revenue Growth and Narrowing Loss

items.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) searched the residence on Friday of Luvkush Kumar, a Superintendent of the Haryana CGST posted in Sector 25, Panchkula, and recovered assets reportedly worth about ₹1.86 crore after arresting him for allegedly accepting a bribe. The seizure included Indian currency notes valued at ₹24.29 lakh and foreign currency notes at ₹15.65 lakh; gold and silver bullion plus jewellery estimated at ₹1.46 crore, which together with the cash brought the total to roughly ₹1.86 crore. Investigators also found documents covering six bank accounts, investment portfolios, life insurance policies, several immovable properties, vehicle ownership records for Kumar and family members, and financial transaction logs. Kumar was caught after a trap operation following a complaint from a businessman who said he had been asked for illegal gratification in connection with GST proceedings against his firm, including avoiding heavy penalties and issuing further demand notices. CBI spokesperson Beena Yadav stated that the accused initially demanded ₹50 lakh, which during negotiations fell to ₹20 lakh before being raised again to ₹25 lakh, at which point Kumar agreed to accept a ₹10 lakh first instalment with the remainder payable later; she said preliminary verification corroborated this demand. The CBI registered an FIR after the complaint and is conducting further investigation.
items.title: ₹1.86 crore in cash and gold seized from Panchkula CGST officer arrested over ₹10 lakh bribe

items.summary: Following her November 11 self-respect marriage to music composer Anirudh Ravichander in Greece, Sun TV Network executive and CEO of IPL franchise Sunrisers Hyderabad Kavya Maran reportedly distributed gold rings as wedding gifts to Sun Group employees. The gesture surfaced after an employee shared a video on X showing the hamper contents—chocolates, an invitation card, and a gold ring—with staff expressing pleasant surprise at receiving rings rather than the anticipated gold coins. An invitation tucked in the box referenced a luncheon scheduled for November 25 as a dedicated celebration for employees. The exact weight and value of the rings remain unconfirmed, and Sun Group has not officially verified how many employees received gifts. Maran married on November 11 at an intimate self-respect ceremony attended by Rajinikanth and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin; it involved garland exchange but omitted Hindu rituals such as sindoor or mangalsutra. A star-studded reception followed in Chennai on November 21. The text notes that all details regarding the employee gifts are based on a single viral video, with no official confirmation from Sun Group on either ring specifications or recipient count.
items.title: Sun Group Employees Receive Gold Rings Following Kavya Maran-Wed Anirudh Ravichander

items.summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report, Kim Jong Un has not responded to contact attempts from President Donald Trump, while Pyongyang continues expanding its nuclear program and strengthening ties with Russia. Trump tried reaching Kim through established phone lines last year without response, then sent a letter that US officials delivered by hand at North Korea's UN mission in Manhattan before it was placed unopened before a US representative. During his recent Asia trip, renewed efforts to arrange face-to-face talks failed because Kim set conditions Washington could not accept; the administration had floated proposals including a possible formal end to the Korean War and an ambiguous statement on denuclearization, though officials said no meeting-brokering effort was underway as of Saturday. North Korea's arsenal reportedly grew from an estimated 20-30 warheads in 2019 to around 60, with Pyongyang developing solid-fuel ICBMs that can reach the US and are harder to track than liquid-fuel systems. The US intelligence community acknowledged Kim has no intention of negotiating away his weapons programs, and a Trump administration official said the White House lacks a detailed policy plan while leaving its North Korea special envoy position vacant—the national security strategy omitted North Korea for the first time since the Cold War ended. On economic grounds, North Korea's economy reportedly grew 3.5% last year (its third consecutive year above 3%), and blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimated North Korea was responsible for 89% of cryptocurrency hacking losses this year versus 15% in 2021, including a Binance heist exceeding $6 billion; Russia vetoed the renewal of UN sanctions monitoring in 2024 while China abstained. The report notes these developments are drawn from WSJ reporting and people familiar with matters rather than confirmed by direct sources.
items.title: Kim Jong Un Ignores Trump Contact Attempts as North Korea Expands Nuclear Arsenal

items.summary: The Network of Women in Media, India filed a rejoinder with the Supreme Court on Saturday challenging the Delhi Police's characterization of its actions during October protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police had described their conduct—removing journalists from protest sites and placing them in vehicles—as crowd control or removal for verification rather than detention or arrest. The media organisation argued that personal liberty cannot be justified simply by refraining from labeling an action as detention, and contended that the right to newsgathering extends beyond accredited professionals with employer-issued identification cards to include independent, freelance, and digital journalists. It further asserted that recording police conduct at public protests constitutes protected newsgathering regardless of duration, format, or platform. Separately, the media organisation disputed the Delhi Police's closure of three women journalists' sexual harassment complaints, noting the force had determined allegations were uncorroborated based on two complainants declining to pursue their cases and CCTV footage showing no assault; it argued that an inquiry conducted by the accused personnel required independence and that a complainant's choice not to proceed does not establish that misconduct did not occur. The report attributes these claims to Live Law, which covered the filing, though specific details of any court ruling or final resolution are not stated in the source material.
items.title: Media Organisation Argues Delhi Police Cannot Frame Journalist Restraints as Crowd Control

items.summary: More than 100 children and 12 adults were hospitalised with suspected food poisoning after eating 'chowmein' (noodles) at a village fair held on Saturday evening in Hiri village, under the Kirnapur police station limits of Balaghat district in Madhya Pradesh. The incident was reported by several visitors who complained of acute stomach ache shortly after consuming the noodles, according to Balaghat Collector Aditya Singh. Initially, 118 children were admitted to the community health centre in Kirnapur; of these, 45 were shifted to the Balaghat district hospital for further treatment while the remaining 73 were discharged after receiving primary care. The 12 adults who fell ill were also admitted to the district hospital's medical ward. Officials confirmed on Sunday that all patients are stable and out of danger, with Chief Medical and Health Officer Dr Shatrughan Singh Dahiya stating they were being treated under doctor supervision. Collector Aditya Singh visited the hospital to check on the patients' condition and directed staff to ensure proper care. The report notes a related incident in which nearly 2,000 people fell ill from suspected food poisoning linked to Indonesia's free school meals program, though this is presented as an unrelated item rather than part of the Madhya Pradesh event.
items.title: Over 100 children hospitalised after suspected food poisoning from chowmein at a village fair in Madhya Pradesh

items.summary: Mexican authorities arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," a 44-year-old leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation (Los Mazatlecos) and one of the FBI's ten most-wanted fugitives, in a military operation near Guasave, Sinaloa. The capture followed years on the run; US agencies had offered a USD 5 million reward for information leading to his arrest, and he had been under indictment in the United States for more than 14 years.
items.title: Mexico captures FBI most-wanted drug lord El Chapo Isidro; cartel retaliation leaves 11 dead in Guasave

items.summary: A 50-year-old unidentified woman was sexually assaulted and murdered inside an unoccupied train coach at Nagercoil railway station in Tamil Nadu on 14 November, with her decomposed remains discovered four days later. Police used CCTV footage to arrest a 31-year-old suspect named Ayyappan. The incident has drawn attention to security deficiencies at railway station yards and the broader law-and-order situation in the state. Separately reported items include a case in Tuticorin, where a 16-year-old Class 11 student was killed following an argument with the accused who then attempted suicide while police investigate; Karnataka High Court granting default bail to Prajwal Revanna in an obscene video case though he remains detained on other convictions; and Prime Minister Modi touring West Bengal, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh promoting development initiatives. The source material is presented as unverified reporting.
items.title: Woman Sexually Assaulted and Murdered at Nagercoil Railway Station; Suspect Arrested via CCTV

items.summary: Following the October election, caretaker premier Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party was tasked with forming Israel's next government. Negotiations between Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu have stalled over who should hold the prime ministership, with reports indicating that Netanyahu remains firm on retaining the office for a full four-year term rather than accepting a rotational arrangement under which Eisenkot would initially serve as PM. Likud conveyed conditions for a possible national unity government through Hebrew media; AFP reported that these leave no room for such a rotation and extend beyond the prime ministership question, including demands for an administration of Jewish-led parties from far-right Otzma Yehudit to left-wing Democrats while excluding both Arab-led parties, plus calls to end personal attacks on Netanyahu, endorse another offensive against Iran, retain Israeli positions in Gaza until Hamas is removed, keep judicial overhaul legislation pending consensus, advance a Haredi military draft bill per the outgoing government's proposal, and hold a political commission of inquiry into the October 7 attack. Eisenkot invited Likud representatives for fresh talks beginning Sunday (November 22), which his party described as an effort to bring in the widest possible grouping; AFP reported this invitation. The three allegations concerning Likud's positions on judicial overhaul, military conscription, and the proposed inquiry have been rejected by Likud, though it did not address its remaining demands. Opposition leaders Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Liberman have ruled out joining Netanyahu's camp or even a rotational arrangement that would let Netanyahu become PM after Eisenkot; Liberman advocated instead bringing ultra-Orthodox parties Shas and United Torah Judaism into the coalition to reach 61 seats for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. However, United Torah Judaism denied reports of negotiation progress while Shas showed little inclination to abandon its alliance with Likud. As an alternative if negotiations fail, Eisenkot could seek a minority government relying on abstention from Ra'am and the Joint List; Liberman rejected this possibility as potentially helping Netanyahu return to power. Eisenkot promised not to let talks drag indefinitely and said he was prepared to put a minority national emergency government to a Knesset vote if broader coalition efforts failed.
items.title: Netanyahu Rejects Rotational Arrangement as Likud Sets Conditions for Unity Government

items.summary: An official, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that Tamil Nadu had signed memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with 112 companies committing investments worth ₹1,14,811 crore over the first 195 days since the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government took office in May. The official projected these commitments would generate approximately 1,32,771 jobs across sectors described as diversified for balanced growth. This announcement preceded a second investors' conclave scheduled for November 25 in Chennai, following the first round held on August 13; chief minister C Joseph Vijay was sworn in on May 10 after TVK won 108 of the assembly's 234 seats and formed a post-poll alliance with Congress, VCK, and IUML. In response to opposition concerns about transparency—particularly allegations that many MoUs were signed during the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) rule—the official said details are regularly shared through Guidance Tamil Nadu or the Chief Ministers' Office, citing a government commitment to accountability. However, BJP and other opposition figures questioned whether investments designated for Tamil Nadu were instead being diverted to Andhra Pradesh; former Puducherry lieutenant governor Tamilisai Soundararajan called on the state industries department to clarify retention measures for existing firms and disclose how many announced MoUs have become operational factories versus new job creation. The report notes these investment claims remain unverified, as no independent confirmation of the figures or their conversion into functioning enterprises was provided.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Reports ₹1.14 Lakh Crore in TVK-Era Investments Amid BJP Questions Over Andhra Diversion

items.summary: CCTV footage of a Saturday morning accident on a highway in Andhra Pradesh's Kakinada district shows an elderly man riding a motorcycle emerge from a service lane and attempt to cross directly into the path of an approaching blue SUV. The SUV driver swerved onto the opposite side of the road to avoid him, colliding head-on with an oncoming white SUV; that impact triggered a chain reaction in which another motorcyclist was thrown several feet into the air. According to the report, two people died and three others were seriously injured and rushed to a nearby hospital for treatment. The identities of both the deceased and the injured have not yet been ascertained, and further details are pending.
items.title: Two Killed in Chain-Reaction Crash on Kakinada Highway After SUV Swerves from Elderly Motorcyclist

items.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar offered to constitute a five-member inquiry committee chaired by BJP state president BY Vijayendra to examine the expenditure on renovating the Kumara Krupa guest house, which was converted into his official residence 'Ganga.' The offer followed Vijayendra's accusation that approximately Rs 100 crore of public money had been spent on the project and allegations that it was carried out without a proper tender process. Shivakumar stated the committee could include members from the BJP, JD(S), and Independents but would not require any Congress member, noting Vijayendra could select MLAs or MLCs within two days. He said the report could be submitted for Assembly discussion during the legislature session early next month. The proposal was made after Vijayendra's Friday questioning of extravagant spending during a drought and requests for clarification on reports that contractors had been instructed to submit bills totalling only Rs 2-3 crore.
items.title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar Offers BJP-Led Committee To Probe Kumara Krupa Renovation Cost

items.summary: Two people of Indian origin were shot dead in a Walmart parking lot in Surrey, British Columbia, on November 15. The victims, identified by the Surrey Police Service as 23-year-old Gaganpreet (Garry) Rehal and 24-year-old Sukhjeet Kaur—who lived in neighbouring Delta—were found with gunshot wounds at around 10:38 pm; first responders attempted resuscitation before both were pronounced dead. The Surrey Police Service stated that investigators believe the shooting was a targeted attack linked to organised crime, according to the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team (IHIT). A red Mustang with its windows blown out was seen in the parking lot by CBC News reporter, and Rehal had prior weapons offences on record while Kaur reportedly had limited known contacts in Canada. Police believe a nearby car fire reported about 13 minutes after the shooting is connected to the killings, with the burnt vehicle considered possibly belonging to the suspect; this attribution was described as believed rather than confirmed. The IHIT said it is investigating the circumstances of the deaths and identifying those responsible, and has appealed for public assistance including CCTV footage and dash camera recordings. All details regarding motive, criminal affiliation, and the identity or role of any suspects remain unconfirmed pending further investigation.
items.title: Indian-Origin Couple Killed in Surrey, Canada; Organised Crime Link Suspected

items.summary: On Tuesday, MS Dhoni announced that he was ending his playing career in the Indian Premier League (IPL), an outcome described by the author as little surprising given the trajectory of his international and franchise careers. Dhoni debuted internationally in 2004 and led India to three ICC titles—the 2007 World Twenty20, the 2011 Cricket World Cup, and the 2013 Champions Trophy—before being inducted into the sport's Hall of Fame in 2025. He had already retired from Test cricket in 2014 and from other international formats by 2020, but remained active for six years playing franchise cricket exclusively for the Chennai Super Kings (CSK), whom he joined when the league began in 2008; CSK is regarded as arguably the most successful IPL franchise under his captaincy. The author's central criticism—that Dhoni retired too late and after recent struggles, leaving a 'bitter taste'—is explicitly framed as an unpopular personal view rather than established fact. Supporting context includes Dhoni being among the oldest cricketers in the IPL, playing for CSK despite squad transitions under Ravindra Jadeja and Ruturaj Gaikwad not panning out, his 2025 statement that he could play 'for as long as I want' even if injured or in a wheelchair, and his subsequent season (at age 44) during which he remained part of the squad but did not play at all due to injuries. The author notes Dhoni will continue with CSK as team mentor, similar to Sachin Tendulkar's role for the Mumbai Indians. No chart is warranted because the text contains no quantified comparison or trend suitable for visualization.
items.title: MS Dhoni Announces Retirement from IPL After 17 Years as a Player

items.summary: During the first Test between India and New Zealand, wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a remark captured on his stump microphone that went viral among fans. The comment—"Yahan se nahi aayega single… She is ready to mingle" (translated as "You won't get a single from here... she's ready to mingle")—appeared to be an observation suggesting the batter could not score off a particular fielding position, combined with a playful English phrase. The text attributes Pant's trademark style of mixing Hindi commentary with punchlines and his animated presence behind the stumps as context for the remark. It notes that this is consistent with prior viral instances of his stump mic chatter, including motivational comments to bowlers and attempts to unsettle opposition batters, though it offers no specific dates or match details beyond identifying the contest as India vs New Zealand. The piece frames Pant's remarks as entertainment value rather than substantive cricketing analysis.
items.title: Rishabh Pant's Stump Mic Remark Goes Viral During India vs New Zealand Test

items.summary: Scientists warn that El Nino-driven sea level rise and king tides are bringing a triple threat of heavy rain, rising seas and high surf to the California coastline this week. The US National Weather Service issued storm warnings on Thursday for dynamic fronts producing rainfall rates over an inch (25.4 mm) per hour, prompting multiple flash flood warnings. An atmospheric river affected by what is being called a super El Nino caused flooding in San Francisco on Wednesday, dumping 2.64 inches of rain in one day and surpassing a record that had stood for more than a century; the storm stranded cars on Bay Area freeways and left more than 51,000 electricity customers without power by Wednesday afternoon. El Nino is described as a climate pattern marked by warmer-than-normal tropical Pacific waters that can bring wetter conditions to California while temporarily raising sea levels along the West Coast, allowing high tides and powerful waves to reach farther inland. Large swells battered Southern California's coast on Thursday, worsening erosion from earlier storms; in October a 360-foot crack appeared in a coastal bluff beneath Pacific Coast Highway near Crystal Cove State Park, prompting Caltrans to restrict traffic to one lane each direction while crews stabilized the slope. A high surf advisory remained in effect for Malibu and Los Angeles County beaches through 9 a.m. Friday with waves of 6 to 9 feet expected. Scientists expect the worst next week when king tides run from Sunday through November 27, potentially accompanied by large swells and further rain; starting Monday maximum coastal water levels in parts of Southern California could exceed 8 feet. Mark Merrifield, director of the Center for Climate Change Impacts and Adaptation at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, warned that California faces a triple threat from higher waves, more rain and higher sea levels associated with this El Nino event. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration estimates roughly a 60 percent probability through October to December of a historic El Nino exceeding every prior event since records began in 1950, while the US Geological Survey states the event is projected to be the largest and most intense on record. In response, Governor Gavin Newsom signed an executive order on October 27 establishing a Highway 1 Task Force to identify vulnerable sections of the coastal highway; emergency project expenditures along Big Sur totalled about $312 million from 2020 through 2026. The article notes it was auto-generated from an agency feed and unedited by FPJ's editorial team.
items.title: El Nino Drives Record Rainfall, King Tides And High Surf Along California Coast

items.summary: On Sunday, November 22 at approximately 6 PM, Uttar Pradesh authorities will run a coordinated mock drill across all 75 districts of the state to test emergency response readiness. Organized by the UP Civil Defence Department in accordance with Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) guidelines, Principal Secretary Samyukta Samaddar stated that District Disaster Management Authorities (DDMAs), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), police, fire services, and the health department will participate. The exercise aims to assess warning systems and evaluate how quickly relevant departments, emergency services, and civil defence volunteers can respond during crises such as war or aerial strikes. Residents may hear air raid sirens lasting nearly two minutes followed by a temporary power blackout while they practice moving to safe locations and taking shelter; an all-clear signal will follow once the simulated threat ends. Samaddar emphasized that residents were informed in advance specifically to prevent panic and curb rumours, consistent with messages shared on social media platforms such as Zee Uttar Pradesh Uttarakhand's Twitter account dated November 22, 2026.
items.title: Uttar Pradesh to conduct statewide civil defence blackout and siren drill on November 22

items.summary: In the early hours of Sunday, November 22, 2026, a vehicle carrying pilgrims returning from Khatu Shyam Temple collided with a parked truck near Shambhupura on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan, killing nine people and injuring several others. According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi, who spoke to ANI, the vehicle was transporting 16 members of one family heading back to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam; all nine deceased were from that same family. Authorities reported that post-mortem examinations are underway for those killed while injured persons receive medical care. A survivor recounted that the group had split into two vehicles en route toward Dhar, and upon receiving a phone call about the crash they rushed to the scene where three vehicles and 36 people were present; this account is not independently corroborated by officials. The article provides no official cause of the collision or details on how many injured survived.
items.title: Nine Pilgrims Killed When Vehicle Hits Parked Truck on Kota-Udaipur Highway in Rajasthan
